title: Sex life: I know the city as only a sex worker can
gist: Sydney sex worker and novelist Tilly Lawless reflects on a country childhood in Bellingen and how years of sex work and nightlife made Sydney feel like home. A personal essay with little market-relevant content.

insights.claim: Tilly Lawless considers Bellingen in rural northern New South Wales, where she lived from age 10 to 19, the place that raised her, outweighing her earlier years in Wollombi and Balmain.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: Personal narrative of rural-to-urban identity; low investment relevance.
insights.locator: I moved around a few times

insights.claim: Lawless says her work as a sex worker, which took her to many suburbs and homes, and nightlife gave her an actively built, rather than passive, sense of belonging to Sydney.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: Colour on how informal service work shapes urban knowledge.
insights.quote: It’s through sex work and nightlife that this city has really come to feel like it belongs to me
insights.locator: I have traversed this city widely

insights.claim: Lawless links her affinity for country music to its grounding in and nostalgia for place, citing Dolly Parton and Kasey Chambers.
insights.speaker: Tilly Lawless
insights.so_what: Cultural colour on place-based nostalgia in music.
insights.locator: Part of my affinity for country music
